## Conclusion
- **Pick: Xiaomi TV S Pro Mini LED 75 2026, wall-mounted** (S$2,199, was S$2,599; Xiaomi Official Store, 3-year on-site warranty) — 75" 4K 144Hz, 704-zone QD-Mini LED, 1700 nits peak, at roughly half the price of tier-one equivalents; the weak built-in speakers don't matter because KEF handles audio.
- **It fits his use**: PS5 Pro 4K120 + VRR, KEF over eARC and Switch 2 at 4K60 can all be connected at once; the only loss is Switch 2's 120Hz mode.
- **HDMI plan**: HDMI 1 → PS5 Pro; HDMI 2 (eARC) → KEF LS50 Wireless II; HDMI 3 → Switch 2.
- **Bracket: Vogel's TVM 5605** (15 mm from the wall, VESA up to 600×400, 100 kg, about £93) — the Singapore box has no wall bracket; Xiaomi's install service (75" fixed, S$161 incl. bracket) **excludes wallpaper walls and third-party brackets**, and this TV wall has joinery + wallpaper, so Patrick installs it.
- **Total wall-mounted depth ≈ 8.8 cm** (body 7.3 + bracket 1.5).
- **Not: buying the China version** — it runs HyperOS rather than Google TV, and 26 kg freight plus returns aren't worth it.

## Criteria
- **4K120 ports**: PS5 Pro needs 4K120 + VRR; only HDMI 1/2 run 144Hz, and HDMI 2 is also the eARC port.
- **eARC + CEC**: KEF switches on/off with the TV and the TV remote controls volume.
- **Wall depth**: thinner looks better; plugs must hide in a recessed box.
- **Blooming**: the sofa is centred, so off-axis halos matter little.
- **Input lag**: about 23 ms with local dimming on, 15 ms off (netzwelt test).
- **Landed price and warranty**: Singapore stock with 3-year on-site cover.

en.## 結論\n- **選：Noctua NF-A12x25 5V PWM（120:
## Conclusion
- **Pick: Noctua NF-A12x25 5V PWM (120×120×25 mm) + bundled USB power cable + a USB-A inline on/off switch**, powered from its own wall USB socket or USB charger, not the PS5. 56.6 CFM, 21.4 dB(A), 0.3 A, 2.07 mmH₂O static pressure — best behind wooden slats.
- **Speed control (optional)**: add a Noctua NA-FC1 knob in series (Noctua confirms it works between the USB cable and a 5V PWM fan).
- **Simplest fallback: AC Infinity MULTIFAN S3** (120×25, 52 CFM, 18 dBA, built-in OFF + 3-speed inline switch), S$51 on desertcart.sg; ~1 mmH₂O static pressure loses more airflow behind slats.
- **Skip 15 mm slim fans**: NF-A12x15 PWM saves 10 mm but is louder at full speed (23.9 dB(A)), lower pressure, and 12 V (needs a USB 5V→12V step-up cable).
- **Skip 140 mm (NF-A14 5V PWM)**: most airflow (82.5 CFM) but the 140 mm frame has no margin in a ~14 cm fan zone.
- **Skip MULTIFAN S7**: dual 120 mm, 24 cm wide — does not fit.

## Is the airflow enough
- CFM ≈ 1.76 × W ÷ ΔT(°C). PS5 Pro ≈ 230 W → ~40 CFM for ≤10 °C rise, ~27 CFM for ≤15 °C.
- Rated CFM is free-air; behind slats expect ~60–70 % (TBC). Door is open while gaming, so intake is not the bottleneck.

## Next steps
- Measure the fan zone: ≥125×125 mm clear and 27 mm deep for a 120 mm fan with pads.
- Align the fan with the PS5 Pro rear exhaust, blowing out.
- Ask Patrick for a USB wall socket (or 13A outlet) inside the TV console near the fan zone.

en.## 結論\n- **兩個陽台都裝、全高（地到天花）、橫向、5 cm 間距的 3:
## Decision
- **Both balconies: full-height (floor to ceiling), horizontal, 5 cm spacing, 316 cable invisible grilles.** Full height closes the opening, so a climbing child cannot get over the top. That matters more than whether the cables can be climbed.
- **One-line spec for the contractor:** "316 stainless 7×7 cable, 2.5 mm core, nylon or Teflon coated (state OD); horizontal at 5 cm c/c, full height; aluminium 6063 powder-coated track matching the window frames; stainless fixings into concrete; SETSCO/SGS tensile report for this cable; warranty ≥ 10 yr anti-rust on cable and ≥ 5 yr workmanship incl. free re-tensioning; installer handles the MCST submission."
- **Get three quotes:** Endo Grilles, Diamond Grille System, CSA Invisible Grille (reasons under 'Installers').
- **Legal:** the MCST cannot refuse a child-safety device but may set its appearance (colour, direction, spacing). Get the Sengkang Grand by-laws or renovation guidelines first.
- **BCA states** that owner-added invisible grilles are not safety barriers. The existing 1.0 m barrier must stay as it is.
- **Kid-room window:** install grilles on openable windows too (window type and opening width TBC).

## Spec differences
| Item | Options | Difference | Pick |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grade | 304 / 316(L) | 316 has molybdenum and resists chloride pitting; 304 suits inland sites with regular care | 316 |
| Core | 2 / 2.5 / 3 mm | Thicker is stronger and more visible; 2 mm is common | 2.5 mm |
| Construction | 1×19 / 7×7 / 7×19 | 1×19 is stiffest, 7×7 in between, 7×19 most flexible (more stretch) | 7×7 |
| Coating | Nylon / Teflon / bare | Coating resists abrasion and UV but ages; bare mono-core holds more tension | Coated, state OD |
| Track | Aluminium / stainless | Usually aluminium 6063-T6; must be fixed into concrete | Aluminium, powder-coated to match frames |
| Spacing | 5 / 7.5 / 10 cm | Singapore has no spacing rule for invisible grilles | 5 cm |

- **Breaking load (all vendor or web claims, and they vary widely):**
  - 316, 2.5 mm, nylon-coated to 3.5 mm: 388 kg minimum (UK supplier spec).
  - Blog table: 2.0 mm 150–200 kg, 2.5 mm 250–300 kg, 3.0 mm 350–400+ kg.
  - Diamond Grille claims 1,000 kg per wire.
  - Rely on a test report for the actual cable.
- **Spacing basis:**
  - BCA requires barriers to stop a 100 mm sphere. Invisible grilles are not statutory barriers, but 5 cm is far below that.
  - No rule separates 5 cm from 6 cm. 5 cm (about 2 in) is the tightest common local spacing; it costs more cable for a smaller gap.
- **Horizontal vs vertical:**
  - BCA counts horizontal members with gaps over 30 mm as climbable toeholds, so horizontal cables can in principle be climbed.
  - At full height there is nothing to climb over, so the local norm, horizontal, is fine.
  - Vertical cables avoid the toehold issue but need a floor track. Ask for both in the quote.
- **Lifespan:** no reliable figure. Treat the warranty period as the lower bound.

## Common problems
- **Sagging:** cables bed in and loosen within 30–90 days, and heat and cold shift tension → put a free re-tension in the contract.
- **Tea staining:** salt and iron particles break down the steel's protective surface layer and leave brown spots. Wipe with fresh water, avoid bleach and steel brushes, and passivate with citric acid if needed.
- **Coating ageing:** nylon and Teflon age in sunlight (years TBC); Teflon resists UV better but costs more.
- **Track:** an aluminium track with stainless screws risks galvanic corrosion. Ask what isolating washers the installer uses.
- **Installation:** one owner had grilles block the aircon condenser and had the balcony redone → confirm aircon service and window-cleaning access first.

## Installers
| Installer | Known | Warranty | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Endo Grilles | Recommended by owners on a forum, quotes on site; All Weather uses a 316 core | Premium Nylon 5 yr; All Weather 7+3 yr; Diamond Rod 15 yr | Blog: from $4.90 psf (fixed) |
| Diamond Grille System | Bare mono-core wire (no coating), higher tension | 15 yr anti-rust | TBC |
| CSA Invisible Grille | 316, typically 2 mm, custom spacing | TBC | $10–18 psf |

- **Market price (2025–26, all from vendors or blogs):** $8–10, $10–18 and $12–18 psf have all been quoted; a standard balcony is about $900–1,800. Go by actual quotes.
- **Warranty norms:** anywhere from 3–5 yr to 10–15 yr.
- **Others:** Elelaurels (5 yr, claims SETSCO), Invisible Grille Concept, Meridian, Secret Furnishing (claims 10 yr, from $8.80 psf).
- **What the quote must state:**
  - Grade, core and outer diameter, strand construction
  - Spacing (c/c) and direction
  - Track material, colour and fixing method
  - Tension or breaking load per cable, with a test report
  - Separate anti-rust and workmanship warranty periods, and how many re-tensions are included
  - How area is measured (psf or per foot) and whether the MCST submission is included
  - Cost to remove and refit the aircon and drying rack

## Look & layout
- **Visibility:**
  - From inside, the cables mostly show against the light or up close; thicker or glossier coating shows more.
  - Colours are black, silver and white. Black reads as less visible from outside; silver blends with the frames (relative effect TBC).
  - Match the track to the window frames; SKG frame colour TBC.
- **Living balcony (~560 wide):**
  - The drying rack is fixed to the concrete ceiling and must still lower. Keep the grille's top track at the outer edge, clear of the rack's plane.
  - The swing moves east–west, parallel to the façade. The seat and chains must not touch the cables at any point of the swing; cables flex inward under load, so measure the clearance on site (TBC).
- **Master balcony:** same spec, full height.
- **Cleaning:** soft cloth with water or mild detergent, then dry. Ask the MCST how outside glass cleaning is arranged.

## Condo rules & egress
- **MCST:**
  - BCA notes that works in strata developments may need MCST approval.
  - STB case law (Zou Xiong): child safety comes first and the MCST cannot refuse without good reason; it should publish design guidelines, and without them must assess each case on its merits.
- **'Condos allow only invisible grilles':** this is common practice, not law. Sengkang Grand's by-laws decide (TBC).
- **Fire:**
  - MHA says residential fire safety relies on fire compartments and staircases; balconies and windows are not statutory escape routes.
  - This research found no SCDF rule requiring residential grilles to be openable (TBC).
  - Firefighters can cut the cables with tools.
  - For balcony access, consider one openable section (costs more).

## To confirm
- Sengkang Grand by-laws: grille direction, colour, spacing, deposit, work hours
- Kid-room window type (top-hung or casement) and opening width
- Window frame colour
- Each installer's cable test report and quote

## Verdict
- **Pick: aluminium louvre bi-fold door, white powder-coat, 2 leaves, top-hung roller + bottom pivot pin, no floor track.**
  - When open, the 2 leaves stack to one side and stick out about half the door width (~40), vs a full 80 swing for a hinged door. Actual projection depends on the leaves and frame; supplier to confirm.
  - Louvres ventilate even when the door is shut; aluminium won't swell, warp or go mouldy.
  - Price: Ho Ho Door lists Premium Louvre Bifold at S$599; HDDoor aluminium louver slide & swing S$610–690 incl. install. Quote for an 80-wide opening TBC.
- **If privacy isn't enough: louvre top, solid (or acrylic) bottom.** Full louvres may show into the room from low angles or with the light on inside; check with a sample.
- **No: PVC folding (accordion) door.** Cheap, but flimsy, loud when closed, and looks temporary.
- **No: carpentry timber louvre bi-fold.** Warps in SG humidity and the slats are hard to clean; price TBC.
- **No: sliding barn or pocket door.** A barn door needs ~80 of clear wall beside the opening, which is where the appliance tower or WashTower is. A pocket door means rebuilding the wall; condo wall structure and MCST rules TBC.

## What it is
- **Name**: louvred / louvre (SG trade: louver) bi-fold door; in a bathroom, a bifold toilet door with louvre. The photo shows 2 leaves of fixed horizontal slats.
- **Materials**:
  - Powder-coated aluminium frame: the local mainstream; waterproof, rustproof, termite-proof.
  - PVC / uPVC: cheaper.
  - Timber / MDF shutter: usually custom-built by a carpenter.
- **Build**:
  - Top track: the roller usually carries the weight.
  - Bottom: a fixed pivot pin in the frame, or a short bottom guide.
  - Between the leaves: a centre hinge, often with a catch to hold the door closed.
  - Frame: aluminium, priced separately.
  - Lock: inside latch or double-side lock (HDDoor Alulux comes with a double-side lock).
  - Hardware: keep each leaf ≤ 10 kg (Gripwell system data).
- **Size**: HDB toilet standard is about 3 × 7 ft (about 91 × 213). HDDoor makes up to 3 × 7 ft and custom-makes other sizes. An 80-wide opening is feasible; measure on site.

## Options compared
| Option | Ventilation / privacy | Durability / noise / cleaning | Price (S$) / space when open |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Aluminium louvre bi-fold** | Best airflow; angled slats block a straight-on view, low angles may see in | Humidity-proof; rollers can loosen, oil them; brush the slats | ~599 (Ho Ho list); projects ~40 |
| PVC folding (accordion) | Solid or small gaps only; opaque | Light and loosens; users report loud closing | ~299 (Ho Ho list); stacks at the jamb, almost no space |
| Timber louvre bi-fold | Same as aluminium louvre | Warps in humidity, needs sealing; slats hard to clean | TBC; projects ~40 |
| Aluminium slide & swing (louver version available) | Louver version ventilates; solid version doesn't | No floor track; more complex mechanism than a bi-fold | Louver 610–690, standard 399–599; still needs swing space |
| Sliding barn / pocket door | Solid, no airflow | Pocket doors can derail; repairs mean opening the wall | TBC; a barn door needs ~80 of wall beside the opening |
| Standard swing door | Solid; ventilates only through an undercut | Most durable and quietest | Aluminium swing 690–899; needs the full 80 swing |

## Where to see and buy
- **Ho Ho Door**: 194 Pandan Loop #07-07 (Pantech Business Hub). Mon–Fri 10:00–16:30, Sat 10:00–14:00. Has the Premium Louvre Bifold and a PVC folding door.
- **HDDoor**: 601 MacPherson Road, Grantral Mall #01-13. Alulux aluminium bi-fold S$490 (delivery and install included, 18-month warranty); aluminium louver slide & swing S$610–690.
- **Door Lab**: Blk 642 Rowell Road #02-115. Slide & swing S$418–768; no louvre model listed.
- **Speedy Decor**: 61 Woodlands Industrial Park E9 (E9 Premium). Aluminium bi-fold S$189–269 incl. measuring, install and old-door disposal; no louvre model listed.
- **Goodhill Enterprise**: 30 Kranji Loop #04-01 TimMac @ Kranji. Its site lists a "Lourved" bi-fold, no price; may be trade/project oriented, TBC.
- **Laminate Door Pte Ltd**: Alulux aluminium bi-fold and louvre slide & swing; address and prices TBC.
- Doorstudio, Toplink, Lian Hin and Sliding door SG: no verifiable louvre bi-fold page found, so not listed.

## Ask Patrick / the supplier
- Is 80 the clear width inside the frame or the wall opening? Does the existing timber frame need to come out for an aluminium bi-fold?
- Do the leaves fold into the room or towards the kitchen? How far do they project? Will they hit the bed, the appliance tower pull-outs or the WashTower door?
- Top-hung roller and bottom pivot pin: does it need a hole in the floor? How are the tiles handled?
- Slat angle and spacing: can someone standing or sitting see the bed? Can it be louvre on top, solid at the bottom?
- Inside lock: lockable from inside, with emergency release from outside.
- White powder-coat code to match the kitchen cabinets and wall colour.
- Warranty length, roller replacement cost, and lead time.
- Whether MCST approval is needed to change the door.

## Risks / TBC
- Quotes for the 80-wide size: TBC with every supplier.
- How private full louvres really are: check a sample.
- Louvres collect dust, and next to the kitchen, cooking grease may settle on the slats.
- The dishwasher auto-open hitting the helper-room door: re-check after switching to a bi-fold.

## Decision
- **Pick: a custom-size solid-wood slatted bed frame from Taobao/Tmall (no headboard or a thin wall-side one, on legs, no footboard), ordered to the spec below.**
  - Outer 152 × 192 (≤ 194 including any headboard); slat top 27 from the floor → sleeping surface about 48.
  - Slats ≥ 7.5 wide, gaps ≤ 7 (Tempur UK limit is 9); centre beam + ≥ 2 centre legs; rubber slat holders or clips to stop squeaks.
  - ≥ 11 clear under the side rails and centre beam so a robot vacuum fits.
  - Side rails no higher than the slats, at most a 1.5 lip, so sitting on the edge is unobstructed.
  - Price and forwarding cost to be confirmed.
- **Backup: a Singapore carpenter built to the same spec** (price to be confirmed), or the Taobao 154 × 194 frame already shortlisted, if it meets the spec.
- **Not: off-the-shelf Singapore Queen frames.** The SG Queen mattress is 152 × 190 and frames are typically 162–167 × 200–205 overall; IKEA SG Queen is 150 × 200 with outer length ≥ 200. Both exceed 154 × 194.
- **Not: a 200-long frame or base under a 190 mattress.** It leaves 10 of bare slats at the foot that get stepped or sat on.

## Tempur base requirements (official)
- **Tempur Singapore**: mattresses must always be placed on a ventilated base, e.g. springs or slats, to prevent moisture build-up; use not in line with the instructions is excluded from the guarantee.
- **Tempur UK**: slats no more than 9 cm apart; sturdy platform tops also work; base must be on feet/legs with free air flow, no valance; sleeping on the floor may invalidate the guarantee.
- **Tempur-Pedic US**: slats ≥ 3 in (7.6 cm) wide and ≤ 4 in (10 cm) apart; Queen needs centre support and 5–6 legs; no traditional box spring (too much give); improper support can void the warranty.
- **Combined ordering spec**: slats ≥ 7.5 wide, gaps ≤ 7, centre beam and legs, raised on legs, no valance, no box spring.
- Warranty: Harvey Norman SG lists 10 years manufacturer's warranty for this mattress.

## Height
- Surface 46–50 minus 21 mattress → slat top 25–29; pick 27 (surface about 48).
- At about 164 cm, lower-leg length is roughly 42–45: feet flat, knees slightly above hips, easiest to stand up.
- Memory foam sinks 2–3 when sitting, so the real seat is a bit below 48; that is why not 25.

## Check before ordering
- **Outer**: W ≤ 152, L ≤ 192; with a headboard, ≤ 194 including it (≤ 2 thick, or wall-mount it).
- **Inner clear size**: if there is a lip, ≥ 151 × 191 so the 150 × 190 Tempur drops in.
- **Slat top height**: 27 (± 1), not the frame's overall height.
- **Clearance**: ≥ 11 under the lowest beam (incl. centre beam); measure the robot vacuum incl. its LiDAR turret and add 1.
- **Slats**: ≥ 7.5 wide, gaps ≤ 7, ≥ 1.5 thick; solid wood or plywood, not bowed sprung slats.
- **Structure**: centre beam + ≥ 2 centre legs; bolted metal joints, not hook-in brackets; felt/rubber feet.
- **Noise**: rubber or plastic slat holders at both ends; re-tighten bolts after the first week.
- **Anti-slip**: with no lip, add a breathable mesh non-slip pad; no non-breathable protector or valance.

## Verdict
- **Pick: YU HOME SMARTLUX LITE** (S$549, list S$899, concrete-ceiling installation included; yuhome.com.sg). 113 × 40 × 6.6 with a one-piece hanging frame that doesn't telescope, so its length always fits the 117 between the cabinet doors and the fan. 25 W dual-tone light with adjustable brightness. No fan, no heater. 2-year on-site warranty, 5 years on the motor.
- **Alternative: 米家智能双控晾衣机 2** (crowdfunding ¥1,399, about S$420–575 landed). It has the strongest light: 50 W, 3000 lm, 2700–5700K, CRI 97. It is 7 cm thick, and the two rods rise and lower separately. The problem is that Xiaomi states brightness and colour temperature are set only in the Mijia App. If you choose it, set 2700K and the brightness once in the App at installation; after that the remote only switches the light on and off.
- **Head to head**: both are slim, neither has a heater, and the prices are similar. SMARTLUX LITE wins on a confirmed length, local installation and warranty, and light control without the App. Mijia wins on a brighter, warmer light and telescopic rods.
- **Rejected: Aqara 智能晾衣机 H1**: the only model confirmed to have brightness ± and colour-temperature ± keys on the remote, but it has air drying, heated drying and UV, draws 750 W, and is 9.5 cm thick.
- **Rejected: 米家智能晾衣机 2 / 3, 米家智能双控晾衣机 (first gen), 米家智能晾衣机 Pro**: dimming and colour temperature are App-only, and the remote has only 4 basic keys. 晾衣机 2 is 9.1 cm thick.
- **Rejected: 米家智能晾衣机 1S, 米家智能隐形晾衣机 双杆2.4米, 米家智能晾衣机 3 Max**: the 1S is 9.9 cm thick; the other two are 2.2–2.4 m long and don't fit.
- **Rejected: Aqara 智能晾衣机 Lite, 邦先生 轻空 M31C**: the Lite has a 20 W single-colour-temperature light; the M31C dims only through the App or voice.
- **Rejected: Philips 3000 Series SDR301, Panasonic JM-BB6AW / JM-EN6UW**: the Philips remote only switches the light on and off. Panasonic installs only through dealers in China and doesn't publish its remote keys.
- **Rejected: PRISM+ Solaris XL, Steigen Solar, GoodLiving Platinum Mini 2.0, GoodWife Lite Mini**: the first three have fans and heaters, and the GoodWife poles extend to 180.
- 好太太, 晾霸, 九牧, 云米, 欧普, 鸿蒙智选: none of their published specs shows a slim, unheated model with remote dimming. No official specs were found for 米家智能晾衣机 3C 柔光版.

## Criteria
- **No fan, no heater**: it is only a hanging rack and balcony light; most laundry is tumble-dried.
- **Light control without the App**: the remote or a wall button switches the light, ideally with brightness and colour temperature too.
- **Thickness ≤ 8–10 cm**: the ceiling is exposed concrete, so the body is in plain view.
- **Length ≤ 117**: runs E–W (parallel to the glass doors), cabinet end 20 from the cabinet doors, other end ≥ 30 from the fan blades.
- **Bright, warm light**: ≥ 2000 lm and down to 3000K or warmer, since it doubles as the main balcony light.
- **Total landed cost**: unit, GST, freight and installation added together.

## Comparison
| Item | SMARTLUX LITE | 双控晾衣机 2 | Aqara H1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thickness | 6.6 cm | 7 cm | 9.5 cm |
| Body | 113 × 40 | ~115 × 45 | 128 × 31.5 |
| Rods | 113 frame | 2, telescopic | 145–247 |
| Fan/heat | None | None | Yes, 750 W |
| Light | 25 W dual-tone | 50 W 3000 lm | 18 W |
| CCT | 2 tones, K n/a | 2700–5700K | Adjustable |
| Remote dim | TBC | No, App | Yes, ± keys |
| Extras | BT speaker | Auto-lower | UV |
| Landed | S$549 installed | S$420–575 | Out |
| Warranty | 2 yr on-site | None | None |

## Do first
- **Before ordering (we WhatsApp YU HOME)**: ask for photos of both sides of the remote to confirm brightness and colour-temperature keys. If they're missing, switch to 米家智能双控晾衣机 2.
- **Order**: buy SMARTLUX LITE at yuhome.com.sg. In the installation booking, state "exposed concrete ceiling, long side parallel to the glass doors, cabinet end 20 from the storage-cabinet doors, centred in the 165 depth". Ceilings above 2.8 m add S$160.
- **Power (tell Patrick)**: with no heater, a standard 13A socket is enough and no FCU is needed. Run PVC trunking from the S-09 socket circuit up to the ceiling to above the middle of the rack, and fit an IP66 outdoor 13A socket there. Paint the trunking the ceiling colour.
- **Remote**: stick it on the wall beside the balcony door, 120 above the floor.
- **Submit a renovation application to the MCST**, listing the balcony ceiling drilling and the surface trunking.

## Risks and to confirm
- **Remote keys**: the site lists adjustable brightness, a remote and an App, but not the key layout (TBC).
- **Colour temperature**: only "dual-tone" is stated; Kelvin and lumens are unpublished. 25 W gives about 2000–2500 lm (estimate).
- **Capacity**: the 113 frame doesn't extend, which suits 1–2 people; fold large duvets to hang them.
- **Open balcony**: YU HOME rates it for indoor use and allows sheltered outdoor spots; keep the body on the inner side out of the rain.
- **MCST rules**: the by-laws may restrict drying laundry on balconies (TBC).

## Control and power (verified)
- **SMARTLUX LITE**: comes with a remote. The site also lists an App, but lifting and the light switch are on the remote. The built-in Bluetooth speaker can be ignored.
- **米家智能双控晾衣机 2**: the official launch says stepless brightness and 2700–5700K colour temperature are set in the Mijia App; the remote only lifts and switches the light.
- **Power**: YU HOME accepts a light point (6 A) or a standard socket. P-06 comes from the S-09 socket circuit, not the ceiling-fan point, and is isolated at the breaker.

## Why the Singapore warranty doesn't matter here
- Buying in Singapore isn't about the warranty; the price is the same. SMARTLUX LITE lands at **S$549** including installation and GST.
- 米家智能双控晾衣机 2 from Taobao: ¥1,399 ≈ S$252, plus S$23 GST, S$45–100 sea freight and S$100–200 for an installer, about **S$420–575**, and you'd still have to find an installer and change the plug to BS1363.

## Conclusion
- **KEF LS50 Wireless II + KC62 is the right upgrade for this room. Buy the KC62 too; it is not optional for movies.** On its own the LS50 WII reaches 45 Hz (±3 dB) and 40 Hz (−6 dB). Erin's Audio Corner found limited output below 50 Hz and called it "excellent but not high output". The KC62 (11–200 Hz ±3 dB) handles everything below 70 Hz and adds headroom.
- **A thin sound usually comes from having no sub, or from the Wall EQ cutting too much bass.** The speakers themselves are not too small.
- **The room is a reasonable fit for moderate levels.** The zone is about 47 m³ (ceiling of 2.6 m TBC) and opens onto the corridor and kitchen. Sound & Vision called the KC62 best for small rooms and moderate levels, testing in a room of about 79 m³. Reference-level cinema volume is out of reach.
- **Adding the KEF XIO and Sennheiser AMBEO Plus does not change the pick.** The XIO is the only real alternative: it has a true centre, Atmos and DTS:X, and can take a KC62. But its stereo width is limited to the 121 cm bar, against 252.6 cm between the LS50 WIIs, and it has less music detail. The AMBEO Plus is out: vocals are vague in AMBEO mode, and it is a 2022 model now selling at clearance prices.
- **The honest trade-off is fidelity over immersion.** The system is stereo PCM 2.0 only, with no centre, surround or height channels and no Dolby decoding. In exchange, the music and dialogue quality is far better: What Hi-Fi rated the KEF's sound 5/5 and the Sony HT-X8500's 3/5.
- **Most stable set-up:** inter-speaker cable through the wall conduit, Ethernet to the primary (right) speaker, RCA from the primary's sub out to the KC62, and the TV's eARC port to the KEF HDMI input with the TV set to output PCM.

## 1. Performance in this room
- **Measured and specified figures:**
  - **LS50 WII:** 108 dB max SPL at 1 m; 280 W + 100 W per speaker.
  - **Erin's Audio Corner:** about 90 dB maximum at 4 m; sweet spot of 80–85 dB at 4 m or 90 dB at 2 m.
  - **At 2.5 m:** about 94 dB per speaker. This is an estimate scaled from Erin's figure by distance, not a measurement.
- **Wall EQ:** the speakers are rear-ported and 8 cm from the wall. The < 10 cm setting cuts the most bass. If the sound is thin, try the 10–50 cm setting.
- **Room modes (calculated):** 30.6 Hz, 52.8 Hz and 66 Hz.
- **Listening angle:** with 252.6 cm between speakers and ears about 1.8 m from the speaker plane (assumed), the included angle is about 71°. That is close to the ideal and works well for a phantom centre.
- **Movies:** the TV must output PCM 2.0; the TV downmixes Atmos and 5.1 to stereo. No dialogue enhancement mode was found (TBC).
- **KC62 integration:** selecting KC62 in KEF Connect applies a 70 Hz high-pass and a 45 Hz low-pass. Set the KC62 to LFE mode with the volume at about 3 o'clock. A KEF trainer suggests raising both points by 10–15 Hz if needed.

## 2. Comparison

| Sony HT-X8500 | 2.1 built-in subs; virtual Atmos/DTS:X | What Hi-Fi sound 3/5, muffled dialogue | eARC; £349 at UK launch; SG price TBC |
| Samsung HW-S801D | 3.1.2 with up-firing drivers and centre; Atmos, no DTS:X; wireless sub | Expert Reviews: clear centre dialogue, front-heavy | Mini HDMI eARC; S$524 sale / S$757 |
| HomePod (2nd gen) ×1 or ×2 | A pair supports Atmos and 5.1/7.1; no sub option | S&V Top Pick; limited max volume | Via Apple TV 4K eARC; S$429 each (2023) |
| HomePod mini ×2 | Stereo, no Dolby; no room-correction mic | Weakest bass and volume | Via Apple TV 4K eARC; S$139 each (2023) |
| KEF XIO | 5.1.2 (12 drivers incl. 6 Uni-Q MX); Atmos, DTS:X, MPEG-H; claimed 34 Hz (conditions unconfirmed); sub out + KW2 wireless, so the KC62 can be added | What Hi-Fi sound 5/5 and an Award: precise, with tight bass but less bass than the Sennheiser, so a sub is suggested. Son-Vidéo: clear centred dialogue; music is wide but has less micro-detail and vocal emotion than separate speakers | One HDMI 2.1 eARC port, no passthrough (the PS5 Pro stays on the TV); mic auto-calibration; £1,999 UK, SG price TBC |
| Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar Plus | 7.1.4 (9 drivers + virtual); Atmos, DTS:X, 360 RA; optional AMBEO Sub (8-inch sealed, 27 Hz) | What Hi-Fi sound 5/5: wide soundfield and strong with music; vocals vague and echoey in AMBEO mode | 2 × HDMI 2.0 inputs (no 4K/120, no VRR) + eARC; 4-mic calibration; Harvey Norman S$1,199 sale (was S$2,299); AMBEO Sub S$1,099 (2023) |

## 3. Verdict and tuning
- **XIO vs LS50 WII:**
  - Switch to XIO + KC62 only if movie immersion and dialogue matter more than music. The 121 cm bar fits the 220 console.
  - For this household's music + movies + PS5 use, with 252.6 cm speaker spacing available, keep the LS50 WII + KC62.
  - The XIO launched in 2025, so there are no long-term reports yet on firmware or eARC stability (TBC).
- Choose the KEF with the KC62. If immersion matters more than fidelity, the Samsung S801D is the better pick instead.
- **Tuning:**
  - **Wall EQ:** start at < 10 cm and step up if the sound is thin.
  - **KC62:** start from the preset, set LFE mode and Wall EQ, then raise the crossover points 10–15 Hz if needed and blend with sub gain.
  - **Placement and room:** keep toe-in minimal, add Treble Trim if the sound is dull, lay a large rug and close the curtains.

## 4. Reliability
- **Inter-speaker link:** use the cable, which runs at 24/192 against 24/96 wireless. Forum dropouts were on the wireless link and caused by interference.
- **Network:** use Ethernet. Firmware v4.0 and v4.1 in 2026 still needed Wi-Fi driver fixes.
- **TV:** use eARC with the TV set to PCM. Owners have reported ARC silence and noise bursts, often fixed by PCM output or a certified cable.
- **Sub:** use RCA rather than the KW1, which has reported dropouts.
- **Firmware history:** fixes cover TV auto-switch and mute, sub wake-up, Spotify, Cast and Roon. **No firmware note mentions eARC, CEC or lip-sync.**
- **Residual risks:** CEC and standby behaviour with the Xiaomi TV (TBC), and no lip-sync adjustment in KEF Connect (TBC).

en.## 結論\n- **選：KEF LS50 Wireless II ×2 上 K:
## Decision
- **Pick: KEF LS50 Wireless II ×2 on KEF S2 Floor Stands, outside both ends of console A (220, default).**
  - 252.6 between centres, about 1.8 m to the seated ears, about 71° included angle, a little wider than the 60° ideal; the phantom centre stays solid.
  - Price: KEF HK HK$18,380/pair + S2 HK$3,580/pair; Singapore price TBC.
- **Subwoofer pick: KEF KC62, beside the right stand.**
  - Reaches 11 Hz and fills in below the LS50 WII's 45 Hz; essential for movies.
  - Price: HK$13,800; Singapore price TBC.
- **Rejected: speakers on the console.** The tweeters would sit too low, below the ears, and the hollow drawer carcass resonates.
- Performance and reliability: see 'TV audio options'.

## Placement
- **Axis:** TV, console and sofa on one axis, 160 from the glass.
- **Stands:** left stand centre about 33.7 from the glass, right about 286.3, each 126.3 from the axis.
- **Direction:** face straight ahead or toe in slightly. The Uni-Q stays smooth off axis; raise Treble Trim if it sounds dull.
- **Rear wall:**
  - Speaker backs 8 from the wall, leaving room for the rear plugs to turn down into the S2 column. The LS50 WII is rear-ported.
  - KC62 back 6 from the wall. It is sealed and side-firing; KEF only asks for ≥ 7.7 between each driver and a wall.
- **Height:** tweeters about 81.

## Connections & settings
- **Primary speaker on the right** (KEF's default right channel).
- **TV:** HDMI eARC to the Xiaomi TV's eARC port with HDMI-CEC on and TV audio output set to PCM. Which HDMI port is eARC on the S Pro is TBC; keep the PS5 Pro off the eARC port.
- **Between the speakers:** inter-speaker cable through the Ø32 conduit, with Cable mode on in KEF Connect.
- **Network:** primary speaker on the 家 (Home) Wi-Fi; the console 5-port switch is full (network decision 2026-11-25).
- **KC62:** RCA from the Sub Out, no KW1.
- **KEF Connect:**
  - Wall distance < 10 cm (Wall Mode); if the sound is thin, try 10–50 cm.
  - Bass Extension on Standard.
  - Selecting the KC62 applies its preset (70 Hz high-pass / 45 Hz low-pass).
- **KC62 unit:** LFE mode, rear EQ on Wall, volume at about 3 o'clock.
- **Sockets:** each speaker and the KC62 plug straight into their own double 13A wall socket (KEF advises against extension strips).

## Risks / to confirm
- Singapore prices TBC.
- Stereo only: no Atmos, centre or surround channels (see 'TV audio options' for the trade-off).
- Xiaomi TV CEC wake/standby and lip-sync TBC.

## Decision
> 2026-11-25: all wall switches are now planned by Patrick (positions, gangs and model); this page’s former switch codes and positions are removed, the rest stands.

- **Pick: Apple Home as the only app + Aqara Hub M3 (Zigbee backbone) + a wired Apple TV 4K as the home hub (S$399; the HomePod mini already owned on standby)** — the scene button, sensors and light strips run Zigbee to M3, bridged into Apple Home via HomeKit; the Apple TV handles remote access, automations, Thread border routing and Matter control.
- **The Frame cannot replace the hub**: the Apple TV on the TV is only a streaming app (plus AirPlay 2); Samsung TVs never appear in Apple Home's home-hub list and are not Apple Thread border routers. Only a HomePod, HomePod mini or Apple TV box can be the hub. The Frame has its own SmartThings hub (with Matter/Thread), but that is a second app and is not needed.
- **Home hub: Apple TV 4K (4th generation, A19, Wi-Fi + Ethernet, S$399) wired to the console 5-port switch (one port)** — wired, steadier than the Wi-Fi-only HomePod mini; it becomes the active hub automatically and the HomePod mini goes to standby. It sits in the console middle bay on S-20.
- **No second HomePod mini**: Apple uses only one active hub at a time; M3 is already a second Thread border router. Buy one later only for bedroom audio.
- **Alternative architecture: everything Matter over Thread, direct** — 86-box Thread switches and UK-plug Thread plugs have almost no local stock in Singapore; revisit in 2–3 years.
- **Rejected: Aqara Home as the main app; extra Hue / SwitchBot / Tuya hubs** — another account and another failure point.
- **Network: UniFi Cloud Gateway Ultra + TP-Link TL-SG1005P (data box) + U7 Lite ×3 + a 5-port switch at the console (≈ S$801)** — the UCG Ultra replaces the HB615 StarHub supplies and runs UniFi Network; details in the decision doc of the camera & Wi-Fi research; without a UniFi gateway APs run in standalone mode, configured one by one, with no fast roaming or remote management. Buy: UI Store SG online, or authorised reseller Win-Pro (38 Jalan Pemimpin #07-04 M38); no shop with display units found.
- **Main-door scene button: Aqara Wireless Remote Switch H1 (Double Rocker), S$45** — single/double/long press per rocker + both together, up to 7 Apple Home scenes; battery about 5 years, no wiring.
- **No UPS**: Singapore's 2024 SAIDI was 0.26 minutes per customer, under 1 minute of outage a year on average.
- **Cameras stay out of Apple Home**: Aqara Camera Hub G350 ×3 in the Aqara app, 24/7 video + audio to microSD, lens retracts when home; HKSV records clips to iCloud only, which does not meet the need.

## Criteria
- **Works offline**: wall switches cut power directly; the scene button runs on the home hub (Apple TV) locally, no internet needed.
- **One app, easy family sharing**: daily use is Apple Home; family are invited with Apple accounts; only the cameras use the Aqara app (admin / member).
- **Singapore stock and warranty**: BS 86 mm boxes, BS1363 plugs, 12–36-month local warranty; imports only when there is no alternative.
- **≤ 2 hubs**: Apple TV + M3 (HomePod mini on standby, G350 as a backup); no other device may need its own hub.
- **Native Apple Home features**: Adaptive Lighting requires HomeKit bridging (lost via Matter bridging).
- **Power-loss recovery**: switches set to power-off memory so lights stay off; no UPS (outages are very rare in Singapore).
- **Long-term support**: models on the market ≥ 2 years and still updated (H1, M3, G350).

## Fans and light
- **Living**: blade plane ≈225 AFF, 35 below the 260 false ceiling. A 35° cut-off cone is 25 in radius at the blade plane; fan radius 66 → light passes through the blades only if a downlight is < 91 from the fan centre. Nearest downlight 124 → all pass, none moved; with a 56″ fan the threshold is 96, still clear. The wall washer and daylight never cross above the blades.
- **2 vs 3 blades**: flicker frequency = blades × revolutions per second; a 2-blade fan spins faster but cuts the light only twice per turn — both land around 5–10 Hz, which is visible. So what matters is that no light crosses the sweep, not the blade count; 2 blades block longer per pass, so any crossing would look stronger.
- **Balcony**: 44″ (Ø112), balcony middle shifted 13 towards the swing; blade tips 34 from the drying rack, ≈68 from the swing ropes (at ±100 the rope is ≈19 off the hook at blade height), 27 to the outer edge and to the glass wall (22 with a 48″).
